verses.text_sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच |
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः |
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca |
dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ |
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya || 1 ||
verses.translation: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, assembled on the sacred field of Kurukshetra, eager for battle, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?
verses.meaning: The opening shloka sets the philosophical and ethical foundation of the Bhagavad Gita. By referring to Kurukshetra as 'Dharmakshetra' (the field of sacred duty and cosmic order), the blind king Dhritarashtra acknowledges that truth and righteousness will ultimately triumph. His ego-bound distinction between 'my sons' (mamakah) and 'the sons of Pandu' (pandavashchaiva) reveals the deep-seated spiritual blindness and partiality that birthed the catastrophic war.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा |
आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanastadā |
ācāryamupasaṅgamya rājā vacanamabravīt || 2 ||
verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Having surveyed the Pandava army marshaled in strategic battle formation, King Duryodhana approached his preceptor Dronacharya and spoke these words.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana's immediate reaction upon beholding the smaller but flawlessly organized and spiritually resolute Pandava forces. Despite boasting a vastly superior numerical count of eleven divisions against seven, Duryodhana's inner insecurity and guilty conscience compel him to seek psychological reassurance from his martial teacher, Dronacharya.

verses.text_sanskrit:
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् |
व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāmācārya mahatīṃ camūm |
vyūḍhāṃ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā || 3 ||
verses.translation: Behold, O Master, this mighty army of the sons of Pandu, skillfully arranged in battle array by your intelligent disciple, the son of Drupada (Dhrishtadyumna).
verses.meaning: Duryodhana's diplomatic cunning is evident here. He subtly attempts to awaken resentment and martial vigilance in Drona by reminding him that Dhrishtadyumna—the commander of the Pandava army who was destined to slay Drona—was nonetheless trained in archery by Drona himself out of noble generosity.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि |
युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi |
yuyudhāno virāṭaśca drupadaśca mahārathaḥ || 4 ||
verses.translation: Here in this army are heroic archers, mighty warriors equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna: Yuyudhana (Satyaki), King Virata, and the great commander Drupada.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana begins enumerating the extraordinary champions standing for the cause of righteousness. He describes them as 'Maharathas'—supreme warriors capable of fighting ten thousand archers simultaneously—illustrating that virtue and valor stand united behind the Pandavas.

verses.text_sanskrit:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् |
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
dhṛṣṭaketuścekitānaḥ kāśirājaśca vīryavān |
purujitkuntibhojaśca śaibyaśca narapuṅgavaḥ || 5 ||
verses.translation: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, and the valorous King of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the foremost and most noble among men.
verses.meaning: The list of illustrious righteous leaders continues. These noble souls, renowned for their integrity, wisdom, and strength ('nara-pungavah'—bulls among men), chose to stand fearlessly on the side of justice and divine truth, regardless of the daunting odds.

verses.text_sanskrit:
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् |
सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
yudhāmanyuśca vikrānta uttamaujāśca vīryavān |
saubhadro draupadeyāśca sarva eva mahārathāḥ || 6 ||
verses.translation: And the valiant Yudhamanyu, the formidable Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu), and the sons of Draupadi—all of them verily mighty commanders (Maharathas).
verses.meaning: Duryodhana mentions the younger generation of heroes, especially the fearless Abhimanyu and the five sons of Draupadi, recognizing that the spirit of righteousness is carried forward by youth of boundless courage and skill.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम |
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibodha dvijottama |
nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tānbravīmi te || 7 ||
verses.translation: Know also, O best of the twice-born (Drona), the distinguished leaders on our side, the generals of my army. I name them now for your information.
verses.meaning: Turning from the strength of the opposition, Duryodhana seeks to bolster his own confidence and that of his preceptor by enumerating the legendary commanders assembled under the Kaurava banner.

verses.text_sanskrit:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः |
अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
bhavānbhīṣmaśca karṇaśca kṛpaśca samitiñjayaḥ |
aśvatthāmā vikarṇaśca saumadattistathaiva ca || 8 ||
verses.translation: Your venerable self (Drona), Grandfather Bhishma, Karna, the ever-victorious Kripacharya, Ashwatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta (Bhurishrava).
verses.meaning: Duryodhana lists the peerless titans of martial science. Bhishma and Drona are revered masters of warfare, Karna is endowed with celestial prowess, and Kripa is renowned for battle victory, presenting an outwardly invincible coalition.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः |
नानाशास्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ |
nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ || 9 ||
verses.translation: And there are many other heroes, well-equipped with diverse weapons and expert in the art of war, who have staked their lives for my sake.
verses.meaning: In an unwitting slip of dramatic irony, Duryodhana uses the phrase 'tyakta-jeevitah' (those who have abandoned their lives). While intending to praise their loyalty, his words prophetically foretell their imminent demise in the service of an unjust cause.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् |
पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
aparyāptaṃ tadasmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam |
paryāptaṃ tvidameteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam || 10 ||
verses.translation: Our army, guarded by the invincible Grandfather Bhishma, is limitless and unconquerable; whereas their army, protected by Bhima, is limited.
verses.meaning: Duryodhana contrasts the vast Kaurava forces guarded by the venerable Bhishma with the Pandava army guarded by Bhima. Commentators note his oscillating psychological state—at once boasting of his numerical superiority while masking deep underlying trepidation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः |
भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgamavasthitāḥ |
bhīṣmamevābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi || 11 ||
verses.translation: Therefore, standing firmly positioned at your respective stations in all divisions of the army, all of you must by all means protect Grandfather Bhishma.
verses.meaning: Recognizing that Bhishma is the supreme pillar and moral shield of the entire Kaurava army, Duryodhana commands all generals to safeguard Bhishma from flanks, knowing that the fall of Bhishma would signal the collapse of their campaign.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः |
सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
tasya sañjanayanharṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ |
siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān || 12 ||
verses.translation: Then, to cheer the heart of Duryodhana, the glorious grandfather of the Kurus (Bhishma), the eldest of the dynasty, roared like a mighty lion and blew his resonant conch shell.
verses.meaning: Perceiving Duryodhana's hidden anxiety, the valiant Bhishma sounds his conch with a roaring blast. It is an act of martial compassion to ignite courage, yet it also solemnly heralds the commencement of the cosmic cleansing of the battlefield.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः |
सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śaṅkhāśca bheryaśca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ |
sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdastumulo'bhavat || 13 ||
verses.translation: Thereupon, conches, kettledrums, cymbals, drums, and horns suddenly blared forth all at once, and the sound was tumultuous.
verses.meaning: Following Bhishma's lead, the entire Kaurava host unleashes a deafening symphony of battle horns, drums, and trumpets, reverberating across the earth and skies to assert their military might.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ |
माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ śvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau |
mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaścaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ || 14 ||
verses.translation: Then, seated in their magnificent chariot yoked with four white steeds, Sri Krishna (Madhava) and Arjuna (Pandava) blew their divine conches.
verses.meaning: The narrative focus shifts to the divine chariot bestowed by Agni. White horses symbolize purity, spiritual luminosity, and cosmic order. Sri Krishna, as the Lord of all fortune (Madhava), sounds the divine call of destiny.

verses.text_sanskrit:
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः |
पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ |
pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ || 15 ||
verses.translation: Hrishikesha (Krishna) blew the sacred conch Panchajanya; Dhananjaya (Arjuna) blew the Devadatta; and Bhima of ferocious deeds blew his colossal conch Paundra.
verses.meaning: Krishna is called 'Hrishikesha'—the inner Master of all senses and minds. His conch Panchajanya represents the roar of cosmic truth. Arjuna's Devadatta ('God-given') and Bhima's thunderous Paundra establish the unyielding moral force of the righteous.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः |
नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ |
nakulaḥ sahadevaśca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau || 16 ||
verses.translation: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya (Boundless Victory); Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
verses.meaning: Yudhishthira's conch 'Anantavijaya' proclaims that victory belongs eternally to Dharma ('Yato Dharmas Tato Jayah'). The twin brothers Nakula and Sahadeva add their sweet and resonant battle calls to complete the sacred fanfare.

verses.text_sanskrit:
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः |
धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
kāśyaśca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ |
dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaśca sātyakiścāparājitaḥ || 17 ||
verses.translation: And the King of Kashi, supreme among archers; Shikhandi, the great charioteer; Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unconquered Satyaki;
verses.meaning: The great righteous kings and commanders on the Pandava side blow their respective conches, affirming their collective resolution to uphold truth and justice.

verses.text_sanskrit:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते |
सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
drupado draupadeyāśca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate |
saubhadraśca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhāndadhmuḥ pṛthakpṛthak || 18 ||
verses.translation: Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, O Lord of the Earth (Dhritarashtra), and the mighty-armed son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu)—each blew their distinct conch shells.
verses.meaning: Every commander contributes their individual divine vibration to the chorus of dharma, creating a unified sonic resonance that sanctifies the field of Kurukshetra.

verses.text_sanskrit:
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् |
नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat |
nabhaśca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādayan || 19 ||
verses.translation: That tumultuous roar, echoing through heaven and earth, shattered the hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya notes that while the Kaurava blowing was noisy, the divine resonance of the Pandava conches struck terror and moral dread into the hearts of the aggressors, whose inner guilt could not withstand the sonic majesty of Truth.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः |
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः |
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
atha vyavasthitāndṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ |
pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ |
hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyamidamāha mahīpate || 20 ||
verses.translation: Then, beholding the sons of Dhritarashtra positioned and the flight of missiles about to begin, Arjuna (Kapidhwaja), taking up his bow Gandiva, spoke these words to Sri Krishna (Hrishikesha), O King:
verses.meaning: Arjuna is adorned with the banner of Lord Hanuman ('Kapidhwaja'), signifying devotion, strength, and victory. Poised with bow in hand at the critical brink of war, he turns to Sri Krishna for guidance.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
senayorubhayormadhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me'cyuta || 21 ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Achyuta (Infallible Lord), please draw up my chariot and place it between the two armies.
verses.meaning: Arjuna addresses Sri Krishna as 'Achyuta'—the One who never slips from His divine status and never fails His devotees. He requests the Lord to position the chariot at the neutral center of the battlefield between the opposing hosts.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान् |
कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
yāvadetānnirīkṣe'haṃ yoddhukāmānavasthitān |
kairmayā saha yoddhavyamasminraṇasamudyame || 22 ||
verses.translation: So that I may observe these warriors assembled here eager for battle, with whom I must contend in this tremendous enterprise of war.
verses.meaning: Arjuna explains his reason for wanting to stand between both armies: to directly scrutinize the ranks of the opposing forces and identify all the commanders and kinsmen against whom he is called upon to fight.

verses.text_sanskrit:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः |
धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
yotsyamānānavekṣe'haṃ ya ete'tra samāgatāḥ |
dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddheryuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ || 23 ||
verses.translation: Let me look upon those who have assembled here to fight, seeking to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra in this battle.
verses.meaning: Arjuna characterizes Duryodhana as 'durbuddhi' (evil-minded), reflecting his initial clarity that the Kauravas represent unrighteous greed and moral corruption.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत |
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
evamukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata |
senayorubhayormadhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam || 24 ||
verses.translation: Sanjaya said: O descendant of Bharata, thus addressed by Gudakesha (Arjuna, conqueror of sleep), Sri Krishna (Hrishikesha) drove that magnificent chariot between the two armies,
verses.meaning: Arjuna is praised as 'Gudakesha'—the master of sleep, sloth, and delusion. Sri Krishna, as the Supreme Charioteer, lovingly fulfills the request of His surrender-seeking devotee and drives the chariot into the center of the battlefield.

verses.text_sanskrit:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् |
उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām |
uvāca pārtha paśyaitānsamavetānkurūniti || 25 ||
verses.translation: Facing Bhishma, Drona, and all the rulers of the earth, the Lord said: 'Behold, O Partha, these assembled Kurus!'
verses.meaning: Krishna purposefully halts the chariot directly in front of Bhishma and Drona—the very persons Arjuna loves and reveres most. The Lord invites Arjuna to confront his deepest attachments, setting the stage for divine spiritual awakening.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄनथ पितामहान् |
आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
tatrāpaśyatsthitānpārthaḥ pitṝnatha pitāmahān |
ācāryānmātulānbhrātṝnputrānpautrānsakhīṃstathā || 26 ||
verses.translation: There Arjuna saw stationed fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and companions,
verses.meaning: Positioned between the two armies, Arjuna sees his entire extended family, mentors, and cherished friends divided across the battle lines.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि |
तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śvaśurānsuhṛdaścaiva senayorubhayorapi |
tānsamīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvānbandhūnavasthitān || 27 ||
verses.translation: As well as fathers-in-law and dear well-wishers in both armies. Surveying all those kinsmen arrayed before him, the son of Kunti (Arjuna)...
verses.meaning: Arjuna surveys the full spectrum of beloved relations assembled on both sides of the battlefield, realizing the intimate bonds that will be destroyed in the conflict.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कृपया परयाविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् |
अर्जुन उवाच |
दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdannidamabravīt |
arjuna uvāca |
dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam || 28 ||
verses.translation: Overwhelmed with profound compassion and grieving in deep despondency, Arjuna spoke thus: 'Seeing these my own kinsmen, O Krishna, drawn up eager for battle—'
verses.meaning: Overcome by intense emotional grief and misplaced compassion, Arjuna breaks down, beginning his heartfelt lament to Sri Krishna.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति |
वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati |
vepathuśca śarīre me romaharṣaśca jāyate || 29 ||
verses.translation: My limbs fail and my mouth is parched; my body quivers and my hair stands on end!
verses.meaning: Arjuna experiences acute psychosomatic distress. The invincible archer who conquered mighty armies now experiences physiological collapse under the weight of emotional grief and moral doubt.

verses.text_sanskrit:
गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते |
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāttvakcaiva paridahyate |
na ca śaknomyavasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ || 30 ||
verses.translation: The mighty bow Gandiva slips from my hand and my skin is burning all over; I am unable to stand steady and my mind seems to reel in dizziness!
verses.meaning: The Gandiva bow, the symbol of Arjuna's martial duty and unyielding strength, slips from his grasp. When the intellect is clouded by attachment, one loses the capacity to wield one's instruments of dharma.

verses.text_sanskrit:
निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव |
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे || ३१ ||
verses.transliteration:
nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava |
na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave || 31 ||
verses.translation: I see adverse omens, O Keshava (Krishna), nor do I foresee any good in slaying my own kinsmen in battle.
verses.meaning: Arjuna begins rationalizing his retreat. He sees ill omens everywhere and declares that no 'shreyas' (ultimate spiritual good) can emerge from the slaughter of one's loved ones.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च |
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा || ३२ ||
verses.transliteration:
na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca |
kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogairjīvitena vā || 32 ||
verses.translation: I desire neither victory, O Krishna, nor sovereign kingdom, nor pleasures. Of what use is a kingdom to us, O Govinda, or pleasures, or even life itself?
verses.meaning: Arjuna questions the very purpose of worldly conquest. He renounces ambition, wealth, and sovereignty, arguing that material rewards are worthless if attained through the destruction of those with whom one wishes to share them.

verses.text_sanskrit:
येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च |
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्ध्ये प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च || ३३ ||
verses.transliteration:
yeṣāmarthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca |
ta ime'vasthitā yuddhye prāṇāṃstyaktvā dhanāni ca || 33 ||
verses.translation: Those for whose sake we desire kingdoms, enjoyments, and pleasures are stationed here in battle, having staked their lives and wealth.
verses.meaning: Arjuna points out the existential paradox of war: the very elders, mentors, and brethren whose joy gives meaning to sovereignty stand ready to perish in the clash.

verses.text_sanskrit:
आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः |
मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा || ३४ ||
verses.transliteration:
ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrāstathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ |
mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ sambandhinastathā || 34 ||
verses.translation: Teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers; maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and all other relatives.
verses.meaning: The enumeration of relationships emphasizes the total interconnectedness of the social fabric. Arjuna feels that severing these sacred familial ties is an act of spiritual and societal self-destruction.

verses.text_sanskrit:
एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन |
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते || ३५ ||
verses.transliteration:
etānna hantumicchāmi ghnato'pi madhusūdana |
api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahīkṛte || 35 ||
verses.translation: Even if they slay me, I do not wish to kill them, O Madhusudana (Slayer of Madhu), even for the sovereignty of the three worlds, let alone for this earthly realm!
verses.meaning: Arjuna declares that no prize in the cosmos—not even dominion over the three worlds (earth, heaven, and netherworld)—could justify raising his weapon against his teachers and kin.

verses.text_sanskrit:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन |
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः || ३६ ||
verses.transliteration:
nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrānnaḥ kā prītiḥ syājjanārdana |
pāpamevāśrayedasmānhatvaitānātatāyinaḥ || 36 ||
verses.translation: What joy could be ours, O Janardana, in slaying the sons of Dhritarashtra? Sin alone will seize us if we kill these aggressors (atatayis).
verses.meaning: According to ancient law, 'atatayis' (felons guilty of arson, poison, theft of land, and abduction) may be slain with impunity. Yet Arjuna contends that higher ethical righteousness transcends retaliatory violence.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् |
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव || ३७ ||
verses.transliteration:
tasmānnārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrānsvabāndhavān |
svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava || 37 ||
verses.translation: Therefore, we are not justified in killing the sons of Dhritarashtra, our own relatives. For how can we be happy, O Madhava, by slaying our own people?
verses.meaning: Arjuna concludes that true peace and enduring joy cannot be constructed upon the ruins of one's own family and conscience.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः |
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् || ३८ ||
verses.transliteration:
yadyapyete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ |
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam || 38 ||
verses.translation: Though they, their minds overpowered by greed, perceive no evil in the destruction of a family dynasty, nor any sin in betrayal of friends,
verses.meaning: Arjuna acknowledges that Duryodhana and his allies are blinded by greed ('lobha'). However, he argues that those endowed with wisdom must not descend to the moral blindness of the foolish.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् |
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन || ३९ ||
verses.transliteration:
kathaṃ na jñeyamasmābhiḥ pāpādasmānnivartitum |
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhirjanārdana || 39 ||
verses.translation: Why should we not, O Janardana, learn to turn away from this sin, we who clearly perceive the grave evil arising from the ruin of a family?
verses.meaning: Knowledge brings ethical responsibility. Arjuna asserts that the enlightened must take the higher road of non-violence rather than participating in collective social ruin.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः |
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत || ४० ||
verses.transliteration:
kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ |
dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnamadharmo'bhibhavatyuta || 40 ||
verses.translation: With the destruction of the family dynasty, the timeless family traditions (Kula-dharma) perish; and when dharma is lost, unrighteousness (Adharma) engulfs the entire lineage.
verses.meaning: Arjuna reflects on sociology and spiritual culture: the family is the crucible where sacred rituals, moral values, and spiritual disciplines are preserved across generations. Its destruction unchains adharma.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः |
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः || ४१ ||
verses.transliteration:
adharmābhibhavātkṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ |
strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ || 41 ||
verses.translation: When unrighteousness prevails, O Krishna, the women of the family become distressed and corrupted; and when women are degraded, O Varshneya, there arises social chaos (Varna-sankara).
verses.meaning: Arjuna emphasizes that the sanctity and protection of women are the bedrock of cultural integrity. War leaves society fatherless and vulnerable, leading to the collapse of ethical order.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च |
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः || ४२ ||
verses.transliteration:
saṅkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca |
patanti pitaro hyeṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ || 42 ||
verses.translation: Social confusion drags both the destroyers of the family and the family itself into misery; even the departed ancestors fall, deprived of sacred offerings of food and water (Pinda and Tarpana).
verses.meaning: In Vedic thought, the living and the departed ancestors are linked through sacred offerings of gratitude. When family continuity is severed, this cosmic communion of gratitude is broken.

verses.text_sanskrit:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः |
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः || ४३ ||
verses.transliteration:
doṣairetaiḥ kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ |
utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāśca śāśvatāḥ || 43 ||
verses.translation: By these evil deeds of the destroyers of the family, causing chaotic confusion, the eternal community virtues and sacred lineage traditions are utterly devastated.
verses.meaning: Arjuna laments the annihilation of civilization's ethical heritage ('shashvata-dharma'), arguing that the scars of total war outlive the battlefield and poison future generations.

verses.text_sanskrit:
उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन |
नरके नियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम || ४४ ||
verses.transliteration:
utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana |
narake niyataṃ vāso bhavatītyanuśuśruma || 44 ||
verses.translation: We have heard from the wise traditions, O Janardana, that for those human beings whose family traditions are destroyed, dwelling in sorrowful darkness is inevitable.
verses.meaning: Citing traditional scriptural wisdom ('anushushruma'—we have heard from ancient sages), Arjuna reinforces his conviction that transgressing moral order brings spiritual ruin.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् |
यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः || ४५ ||
verses.transliteration:
aho bata mahatpāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam |
yadrājyasukhalobhena hantuṃ svajanamudyatāḥ || 45 ||
verses.translation: Alas! What a grave sin we are resolved to commit, that out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom, we have stood prepared to slay our own kinsmen!
verses.meaning: Arjuna expresses deep remorse and anguish. He looks inward, confronting the potential complicity of his own side in greed and violence.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः |
धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् || ४६ ||
verses.transliteration:
yadi māmapratīkāramaśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ |
dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet || 46 ||
verses.translation: Far better would it be for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, should slay me in battle while I stand unresisting and unarmed!
verses.meaning: In the ultimate declaration of pacifist surrender and inner despair, Arjuna resolves to drop his weapons entirely, preferring his own death over the destruction of others.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः सङ्ख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् |
विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः || ४७ ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
evamuktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopastha upāviśat |
visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ || 47 ||
verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus on the battlefield, Arjuna cast aside his bow and quiver of arrows and sat down upon the seat of the chariot, his heart overwhelmed with sorrow.
verses.meaning: The climactic concluding verse of Chapter 1. Arjuna collapses upon the chariot seat, casting down his divine bow Gandiva in profound despondency ('shoka-samvigna-manasah'). This total breakdown of human ego and pride becomes the fertile soil in which the divine nectar of Sri Krishna's Gita will blossom in Chapter 2.
